caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 61 of 1982
lawyer:
Shafiqur Rahman with Habibur Rahman Khan ------ For the Appellants
Khan Saifur Rahman with Badruddin Ahmed  ------ For the Respondent.
parties:
Anil Kumar Sarker & ors ------Appellants
Vs.
Sree Sree Kalimata Bigraha ------Respondent
full_judgment:
M. H. Rahman, J.—This appeal has arisen out of a suit for declaration that the suit property comprising 10 acre of land of plot No. 140 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No. 52 of Mouja Porrah, P.S. Manikganj is a debuttor property belonging to the deity Kali. Narayan Kumar Datta, a person interested, filed the suit on behalf of the deity. The plaintiff's case is that the suit property was made debuttor by Tara Prosad Sarkar and his brothers. The Sarkars created a temple on the burning place of the dead body of their father, installed the deity and gifted the suit property orally and handed over possession to the deity. They used to perform Puja and other functions and subsequently, they appointed one Hemangini Guha as the Shebait. The Suit land was correctly recorded in the S.A. Khatian. The Sarkers created two tin sheds for the Shebait. Later one Kumud Chandra Roy Chowdhury erected one Chouchala tin shed for the residence of the Shebait. When Hemangini Guha became old she brought her sister's daughter Charu Bala, defendant No. 3, for assisting her in the seba puja. Before her death she created in collusion with defendant No. 3, a will. Defendant No. 3 obtained a probate and gave power of attorney to defendant No. 1, Anil Kumar Sarkar, who on the basis of the Power of Attorney created a registered deed of exchange on 10.10.1980 in respect of the suit property in favour of his wife defendant No. 2. It was alleged in the plaint that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 would remove the idol and after selling the suit property they would leave for India. 

 5. It is clear, there is no satisfactory evidence as to the making of the oral dedication. The facts, however, remain that there is deity in the suit property for about fifty years and the people of the locality make their offerings to the deity there. Lack of the personal knowledge of the plaintiff witnesses as to the exact time of dedication is understandable as it happened long ago. The documents on record, however, lend full support to the assertion of the plaintiff. In the S.A. record of right (Ext. 1) at the column of the owner it is written সেবাইত সূত্রে হেমাংগিণি and the plot is described as কালী বাড়ী The defendants failed to suggest any good reason why Narayan Kumar Datta got the property wrongly recorded in the name of the shebait. It appears, the defendants, for the first time in this proceeding, have tried to make out a case that Hemangini Guha herself took settlement from the Sarker brothers as her personal property. In the recital of the will (Ext.E) Hemangini stated that “সরকার মহাশয়গণের পিতার শ্বশাণে প্রতিষ্ঠিত মাঠ স্থাপিত কালী মাতার অর্চনাদী করিয়া জীবন যাপন করিতেছি।” She did not claim to have obtained settlement from the Sarkers. By the will she appears to have bequeathed the tin-structures on the suit plot. In the will it is written that in case the Sarkars do not permit Charu Bala to stay on the property then she would be entitled to transfer the properties of Hemangini Guha. Obviously her movables were disposed of by the will. In Ext. F, the power of attorney, Charu Baia Sarkar described the property as উক্ত বিগ্রহের সম্পত্তি She did not claim the property to be a settled land of Hemangini Guha. In Ext. A(I), the certified copy of the attached khatian of suit plot, we find same thing was written, in the title column above the entry of the name Hemangini Guha as possession but that portion is torn. A portion of the remark column was also found to be erased. In the Dakhila Ext. B and B(b) some writings in the column প্রজার নাম have also been erased, In rent receipt Ext. A(4), there is also some erasing. Apart from any good documentary evidence, there is no oral evidence in support of the defence contention that Hemangini took settlement from the Sarkars. D.W. 1 stated in cross-examination that he was not present either at life, time of talk of settlement or at the time of the settlement of the suit land. D.W. 2 stated that he was present at the time of talk of the alleged settlement. According to him premium was fixed at Tk. 15/- and annual rental 5 annas some gandas: Ext. A(1) indicates  that the superior interest of the suit holding used to be held by Abdus attar and others under the suit khatian No. 81 (ka) and 81(kha) under kharija Taluk of Joydev Sen at a rent of 5 annas. The defense case that the. Sarkars gave settlement of the suit land at 5 annas and some gandas does not inspire any confidence. D.W. 3 claimed that he was present at the time of settlement. According to him at that time of settlement he was 16/17 years and he was attracted by the persons who went to the house of Sarkers. The defence case of Hemangini's taking settlement from the Sarkars can hardly be relied upon. There is evidence on record that the Sarkars had sufficient landed property in this country, and it is difficult, to believe that they would settle away the suit property comprising the burning place of their father's dead body to Hemangini Guha.
